headline: The beaches that feed orcas
body: Choices made on the shoreline affect the entire marine food web, from forage fish to orca.

headline: Forage fish feed the marine food web
body: Surf smelt and Pacific sand lance lay their eggs in sand and small gravel, on the upper third of the beach.

headline: Shorelines are a nursery for salmon
body: Young salmon feed, grow and shelter along these shores on their way to the open ocean.

headline: Critically endangered orca
body: Southern Resident orcas rely almost entirely on Chinook salmon. Their survival depends on abundant fish from healthy habitats.

headline: Feeder bluffs are beach builders
body: {{shoreline.shoreform_feeder|1}} miles of feeder bluffs supply the sand and gravel that build beaches. Hard armoring starves nearby beaches.

headline: Rebuilding resilient shores
body: Friends is restoring marsh and beach habitat here, where sand lance eggs were found in 2018 and 2019.

headline: Protect this Place with us
body: 6,000 feet of shoreline restored for forage fish and eelgrass. Small actions on your own shore can make a big difference.
